text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Severity=P1 - multiple containers in `prefill` group restarted repeatedly on gpu-pool-rtus-5. Symptoms: OOM during prefill, gradual node flaps. Pager routed to #incidents and @sre-oncall. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/prefill-oom

sre-oncall: I'm on it. seeing a burst of prefill jobs with huge context lengths arriving ~04:12 UTC. kube events show repeated OOMKills for containers in deployment redwood-prefill-rtus (replicas 12 -> flapping).

marco: I grabbed a timeline — Prometheus shows GPU memory usage jump from 40% -> 100% on three nodes at 04:11:55. p99 prefill time spiked and then containers restarted. Looks like long-prompt workloads (user payloads > 200k tokens) are hitting us.

anna-eng-runtime: logs from one pod (runtime-rtus-5f7b):
```
I0414 04:11:58.123 runtime.cpp:456] prefill: incoming request id=req-9a3f
prefill_alloc: requested 24.5GB, available 22.0GB
E0414 04:11:58.124 cuda_memory_manager.cpp:89] OOM allocating 24500000000 bytes
E0414 04:11:58.124 runtime.cpp:462] Container exiting with SIGKILL (OOM)
```
That matches OOM at allocation time during tokenization/prefill. Not a driver crash; just exhausted allocated device memory.

sre-oncall: Which customers are affected? any public-facing endpoints degraded?

katie-cs: Support reports spike in 503/504s for a small set of customers using large-context beta. CS ticket INC-2026-447 opened. Approx 0.9% of total requests affected but for those tenants it's high-impact.

marco: Quick mitigation plan: 1) apply immediate backpressure on edges that accept very large contexts (enforce max_context_size=64k). 2) Route large-context traffic to lower-memory model variant (redwood-2-small) temporarily. 3) Increase node eviction threshold to avoid noisy restarts.

anna-eng-runtime: I can push a config override to the API gateway to reject requests with context_size > 65536 tokens. Command to preview: 
```bash
redwoodctl config set gateway.max_prefill_tokens=65536 --env=prod --preview
```
If approved I'll promote to live.

sre-oncall: Do it. Also start scaling down prefill replica autoscaler to reduce simultaneous prefill concurrency: kubectl scale deployment/redwood-prefill-rtus --replicas=6 -n inference-prod

anna-eng-runtime: Applied preview then promoted. Gateway now rejects overly-large prefill requests with 413. Pushing scale down.

incident-bot: Action taken: gateway config updated, deployment scaled to 6 replicas. Notified all watchgroups.

marco: After gating large requests, GPU memory usage dropped and no new OOMKills for 10m. p95 latency returned to normal. We still have 2 nodes with residual fragmentation — recommend cordon/drain + rolling restart to reclaim fragmented GPU memory on those hosts.

sre-oncall: I'm cordoning node gpu-rtus-5b: `kubectl cordon gpu-rtus-5b` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-rtus-5b` — scheduling maintenance now.

product-oncall: Any customer-visible mitigations we should tell CS to communicate?

katie-cs: Tell customers we applied stricter context limits temporarily and routed very-large-context requests to fallback models to keep latency stable. We're working on a permanent limit and better backpressure.

anna-eng-runtime: Follow-up work logged: RT-3124 (prefill allocation safe-guards), RT-3125 (gateway-side token counting + rejection), RT-3126 (auto-fallback to quantized model variant when mem pressure). I also left a hotfix branch that rejects prefill > 64k upstream of tokenizer.

sre-oncall: Current status: mitigations applied, traffic stable, no new restarts in last 15m. Severity -> P2 for now. Still tracking until nodes fully drained and restarted.

marco: Noted an odd pattern where some requests with moderate token counts still caused large allocation due to token streaming metadata — adding instrumentation to tokenization to report raw token vs allocated bytes.

incident-bot: INC-2026-447 created and linked: https://go/incidents/INC-2026-447. Postmortem template assigned to @anna-eng-runtime and @marco.

sre-oncall: Handoff: I'm handing this to @night-oncall in 2 hours. Summary for next on-call: 1) gateway cap at 64k enforced 2) deployment scaled down to 6 replicas 3) two nodes (gpu-rtus-5b, gpu-rtus-5d) are drained and will be restarted; watch for repeat OOMs after they rejoin 4) CS notified and customers informed 5) follow-ups RT-3124/3125/3126. If OOMs reappear, revert gateway change to allow diagnostic traffic and escalate to eng-runtime.

night-oncall: Ack. I'll monitor overnight. Please paste the cordon/drain outputs and the list of impacted customer request IDs into the incident ticket before handoff end.

katie-cs: Adding customer IDs and sample request ids to INC-2026-447 now. Also posting customer-facing note draft: "We identified and mitigated a production issue where very large context requests caused GPU memory exhaustion and container restarts. We've applied temporary limits and routing to keep services stable; engineering is working on a permanent fix."

sre-oncall: Final note before sign-off: node flaps appear triggered by sustained prefill allocations that cause fragmentation rather than one-off huge single allocation. Long-term: add allocation compaction and per-request accounting + early failure. I'll update the runbook with these steps. Handoff complete.

night-oncall: Thanks — monitoring alert rule adjusted to send me a direct page if OOMKills > 1 in 10m. Signing on.
